title: Surgically altered ciliate cortex is inherited across generations despite wild-type DNA

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Surgically altered ciliate cortex is inherited across generations despite wild-type DNA

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In unicellular ciliates, changes made to cell-surface form can be inherited across generations independently of DNA: surgical rotation of a small patch of cortex creates a stable line in which part of the ciliary beat pushes food out of the mouth, which the wild-type genome cannot correct.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Multiple modalities for computation and control across scales

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Changes made to unicellular form can persist across generations [203–205]; for example, surgical rotation of a small patch of the cell surface creates a stable line of animals in which a portion of the ciliary beat pushes food out of their mouths—a condition which their perfectly wild-type genome cannot correct.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Multiple modalities for computation and control across scales”. Scope: Ciliates such as Paramecium and Tetrahymena

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The intervention, inherited phenotype, and predicted feeding effect are direct and discriminating. The limiting factor is public availability and resolution of historical experimental records rather than conceptual testability.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Trace surgically rotated cortical landmarks, ciliary orientation, feeding flow, and genotype through clonal generations without further intervention. Persistent rotated organization and reversed local flow despite wild-type sequence support non-DNA cortical inheritance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cytoplasmic inheritance mechanisms other than cortical geometry remain possible.

Sequence confirmation may be absent.

Classic experiments may lack accessible raw films or lineage-level data.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.62
data existence: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.38
discriminating power: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cortical rotation, inheritance across fissions, and failure of the nucleus to restore normal feeding are concrete and were reported repeatedly in the ciliate literature. Reference genomes exist, but not for the operated lines, so the wild-type-DNA clause cannot be rechecked from sequence. The anatomical inheritance can be assessed from the published experiments, with the limits of pre-genomic records.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track ciliary beat direction and feeding after a 180-degree cortical rotation in Paramecium or a related ciliate, across asexual generations, and sequence the same lines. Inheritance of reversed beating with a genome that matches the unoperated stock would support cortical inheritance that the genome does not correct; loss of the reversal within a few fissions, or a fixed nuclear mutation, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The classical lines were not sequenced, so wild-type DNA is inferred from genetics rather than from a public genome of those cells.

The primary observations are journal descriptions from the 1960s onward, not a single downloadable pedigree.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.8
data existence: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.62
